label: Pre-copy (t>=2 through <DEL>) when the sequence starts with g/u/p/3/2/i/b/j, on non-digit, non-set inputs
explanation: Fires almost entirely before the copy: during the original phase from t>=2 (never at t=0,1) and especially on <DEL> (24% of <DEL> steps, 46% of mass). The copy phase holds only 9% of mass. What drives it is which tokens started the sequence: the first original token (and to a lesser extent the second) being g, u, p, 3, 2, i, b or j raises the rate about 2-3x. The top activations (about 0.41) are <DEL> steps in short sequences that start with g or u. Within the original phase it fires on letter inputs that are not in that set (k, v, a, w, n, d, r ...) and rarely on digits or set tokens. It is weaker on later steps of long sequences and does not fire at t=0 or t=1. The response is graded: having more set tokens in the prefix raises the rate, but no single clean rule exists, and many qualifying steps stay below threshold, so precision is about 0.36.
